How the numbers are made

  • Benchmark: per model, the best score among the rows the chosen sources allow (labs usually report their best setting; the setting is in the evidence table). Scores in % or 0–1 are used; Elo and other scales are shown but not rolled up.
  • Everything above a benchmark: the mean of its parts, weight 1 each, over the parts measured for that model. "k/n" = parts measured of the parts that have any data. A model is ranked only if it has at least the chosen share of parts.
  • Compare: the table under the ranking compares the models you pick (click a bar to add or remove). "Only parts all of them have" recomputes every number on the same parts for all compared models, which is the fair comparison.
  • First version: all weights are 1 for now, and where a benchmark sits in the tree is a first placement; both will change. Numbers are as the labs and leaderboards published them, read from their pages and checked by script against saved copies of those pages; a random sample of 60 was re-checked by a second model for the right model column (no errors found).
  • Code optimisation: our Quern runs (Claude models only): a technique counts 100 if the model used it in at least one run, else 0.
  • Sources: "labs about own models" = launch posts, model and system cards of the model's developer. Numbers a lab published about a competitor and third-party leaderboards are added by the switch. Data from Artificial Analysis' own files is not used.
